A tab character that reaches the value by a paste (TXI-56) or from the product SHALL be kept and drawn as TXI-54 says, and SHALL be removed by Backspace or Delete as one character.
behavior.verify: Focus a multi-line code field between two buttons: Tab moves focus to the next button and Shift+Tab to the previous one, and the value is unchanged. Enter after an indented line adds a line break and no other character. A value set to a tab and a letter: Backspace after the tab leaves the letter alone; typing ( or " inserts that one character.

behavior.text: WHILE type is code THE text input SHALL be exposed to assistive technology exactly as the text input of its other types is: a text box — a multi-line one WHILE multiline is true — named and described as TXI-23 says, and invalid, required, read-only or disabled as TXI-5, TXI-10, TXI-11 and TXI-23 say. It SHALL add no role, no role description, no word and no announcement for holding code, because Tanrei has no words (TXI-52) and what the field expects is said by the product in the label and the help of its Field; it SHALL expose the value character for character, with no part of it marked as misspelled; it SHALL keep the caret's and the selection's reporting to the platform's text element; and it SHALL NOT announce that a line wrapped or that the input scrolled.
behavior.verify: The accessibility tree of stacked-code-multiline is that of the same field with type text: a multi-line text box named by label, with no role description, and the inner element carries no aria-roledescription and no aria-label that the other types do not.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform draws with a person's own forced colors THE text input SHALL draw a code field as it draws any field of its variant — its edge, its value and its placeholder in the platform's colors, the focused edge in the platform's highlight color — and nothing more: the code face, not a color, is what tells code from words. WHILE the text size is enlarged a code field SHALL grow with its text as TXI-16 and TXI-37 say, the code face keeping the input's size; at twice the text size in a container 320 wide a multi-line code field SHALL wrap (TXI-57) or scroll inside its container (TXI-58), a single-line one SHALL scroll within its line as every single-line field does, the floating label SHALL wrap (TXI-13), as the rows of its Field do (FLD-16), no content SHALL be cut, and the page SHALL NOT scroll sideways.
behavior.verify: With forced colors emulated, stacked-code-multiline differs from the same field of type text in its font family alone. At a root font size of 200 % in a container 320 wide, stacked-code-multiline-wrap, stacked-code-multiline-nowrap and stacked-code: the document does not scroll sideways and no text is clipped by the container.

behavior.text: THE text input SHALL say to the Field that frames it what only the input knows, and SHALL say it again WHEN it changes: that it draws the label itself WHILE its variant floats one (TXI-13), so that the Field draws no label row (FLD-25); how far its text stands from its own start edge — its inline padding and, beside a leading icon, that icon and its gap (TXI-16, TXI-22) — and the padding it keeps at its end edge (TXI-16), so that the Field's supporting row starts and ends there (FLD-26); and an entry error with its words (TXI-30, FLD-28). Its count is not among them: the Field is given a count as words (FLD-27), by what holds the two (TXI-19). It SHALL take from that Field its name, its description and its required, invalid and disabled states (TXI-5, TXI-11, TXI-23), whether the label is hidden (TXI-13) and whether an asterisk follows it (TXI-50), so that a Field and a text input placed by hand are drawn, named, described and marked exactly as a text field is.
behavior.verify: The twin test of the text field: each fixture text-<id> of the Field — a Field around a text input, written by hand — is the same picture and the same accessibility tree as the text field's fixture <id>. Unit: changing variant from stacked to outlined removes the Field's label row and floats the same text in the input; adding a leading icon moves the start of the Field's supporting row to the input text.

behavior.text: THE text input SHALL draw no label row above itself, no requirement tag, no help, no error text and no count: those are the rows of the Field that frames it (FLD-2 to FLD-7, FLD-27). WHILE no Field frames it THE text input SHALL be complete as a bare control — its box, the label that floats in it where its variant floats one, everything typed in it, its states and its events — THE text input SHALL be block-level, framed and bare alike: exactly as wide as the place it stands in — the width its layout gives it, which inside a Field is the Field's whole width (FLD-1), so that the box fills its Field — with no width of its own, never the platform's default width for a text element, and never the width of what it holds (TXI-58); the one width it keeps of its own is the one a person gives it with the resize grip (TXI-39). It SHALL be exactly as tall as its container, and the room TXI-13 keeps above an outlined one. A product that wants a narrower box gives it a narrower place.

WHILE the entries slot holds content THE text input SHALL lay that content and its typing part out inside the container, between the leading and the trailing parts, in lines from the start edge: each item comp.text-input.entries.gap after the one before, a line comp.text-input.entries.row-gap below the one above, every item centred on the middle of its line, an item that does not fit going whole to the next line and never wider than a line. The typing part SHALL follow the last item on its line and take what is left of it WHILE that is at least comp.text-input.entries.typing-min-width, and otherwise a line of its own. The container SHALL keep its height while one line fits and grow by whole lines after that, its paddings unchanged.
behavior.verify: The Field's fixtures entries-email-entries (one line), entries-email-many (twelve items on wrapped lines) and entries-email-long-entry (an item as wide as a line).

behavior.text: WHILE the entries slot holds content THE text input SHALL treat itself as not empty for its label: a filled or outlined input floats it (TXI-13), and its placeholder is not shown.
behavior.verify: The Field's fixtures entries-email-filled (floated) and entries-email-filled-empty (resting).

behavior.text: WHEN the user presses the container outside every item of the entries slot THE text input SHALL treat it as a press on the container (TXI-8). THE text input SHALL give the items of the entries slot no role, no focus order and no key: they are the product's, or those of the component that holds the input.
behavior.verify: Unit: a press in the gap between two items focuses the typing part; Tab reaches each item as the item itself decides.

behavior.text: WHILE type is email, url, tel, number or password — a value THE text input lays out left-to-right whatever it holds (TXI-24) — THE text input SHALL treat the prefix, the value and the suffix as one run of writing and SHALL lay the three out in that order along the run's own direction in every layout direction, as the number input does (NMI-39): the run's direction SHALL be that of the first strong character of prefixText and, WHERE prefixText has none, of suffixText — a letter, or a direction mark the product wrote there — and left-to-right WHERE neither has one, so that "$ 120 USD", "https://" before an address and "@example.com" after a name stand in a right-to-left layout as in a left-to-right one, and a unit written in a right-to-left script stands at the value's left. THE text input SHALL decide that direction from prefixText and suffixText alone, never from the value. The value SHALL stay aligned to the field's start edge (TXI-24), and the icons, the picker button, the floating label and the paddings SHALL follow the layout. For every other type the value's direction is the person's and may change at any keystroke, so the row SHALL NOT follow it: the prefix stands at the field's start edge and the suffix at its end edge (TXI-24); a code field's row is TXI-53's, and a date, time or date-time field draws no affix (TXI-28).

THE text input SHALL draw its box from the one set of tokens every input box is drawn from, the group comp.input-box (comp.input-box.container.shape, comp.input-box.container.height.medium, and so on): its container, its corners, its edges and their widths, the label that floats in it and the asterisk after it, the typed text and the placeholder, the prefix and the suffix, the icons at either end, the caret and the highlight of selected text, the paddings, the gaps and the least height of its size, and the colors of each of these in its look, at rest, hovered, focused and disabled, plain and in error. It SHALL have no token of its own for any of them: the tokens of its own group are those of what only a text input draws — the resize grip (TXI-39), the motion of a height that follows its text (TXI-38), a segment of a date or a time (TXI-42), the code face (TXI-53) and the entries place (TXI-64). WHEN a design system or a product sets a token of the box THE text input SHALL follow it, as the select, the combobox, the number input and the color input do, which read the same tokens; no token is held equal to another for this. WHERE one text input is to differ from the other boxes of a product, the token is set for that instance — on its element or on a subtree that holds it, in each platform's way of setting a token for a subtree — and THE text input SHALL draw itself from the value it finds there.
behavior.verify: Every value the box of a text input draws is the value of the token it reads, in every scheme of every shipped system. A build test fails if a token with the name of a token of the box stands in the text input's own group. Unit, web: with the custom property of comp.input-box.container.shape set on one text input's element, its corners change and those of a text input and a select beside it do not; set on an ancestor of the three, all three change.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the input; further Tabs move to an interactive element in the trailing slot, then to the picker button, then to the resize grip, where there are any. In a date, time or date-time field Tab visits each segment in turn first. In a code field too: Tab never inserts a character or an indent (TXI-59).

keyboard.keys: Typing, Backspace, Delete, arrows, Home, End, selection and clipboard shortcuts
keyboard.action: Edit the value as the platform's own text element does (types other than date, time and date-time).
In a single-line field, commits the value and emits action (and submits the enclosing form on the web). In a multi-line field, inserts a line break.

keyboard.keys: Arrow keys, Home, End in a multi-line code field whose lines do not wrap
keyboard.action: Move the caret as in any text; the input scrolls sideways to keep it in view (TXI-58).

keyboard.keys: Left Arrow, Right Arrow on a segment
keyboard.action: Move focus to the segment drawn to the left or to the right (TXI-43).

keyboard.keys: Up Arrow, Down Arrow on a segment
keyboard.action: Raise or lower the segment by one, wrapping; fill an empty segment from the current date or time (TXI-44).

keyboard.keys: Page Up, Page Down, Home, End on a segment
keyboard.action: Step by a larger amount; go to the first or the last value of the segment (TXI-44).
Fill the segment and move to the next once it can take no more; the separator's character also moves on (TXI-45).

keyboard.keys: Backspace or Delete on a segment
keyboard.action: Remove the segment's last digit; Backspace on an empty segment moves to the previous one (TXI-45).

keyboard.keys: Paste, copy and cut on a segment
keyboard.action: Paste reads a whole date or time into every segment; copy and cut take the whole row (TXI-29).

keyboard.keys: Enter or Space on the picker button
Up Arrow, Down Arrow, Home, End on the resize grip
keyboard.action: Make the field one line shorter or taller; return it to minRows or take it to its tallest (TXI-41).

keyboard.keys: Left Arrow, Right Arrow on the resize grip
keyboard.action: Where the field resizes both ways, narrow or widen it; the arrow toward the end edge widens (TXI-41).

keyboard.keys: Enter or Space on the resize grip
keyboard.action: Fit the height to the text, or return to minRows when it already fits (TXI-41).

accessibility.labeling: The accessible name is the label of the Field that frames the input, or its own label where no Field does; a filled or outlined input draws that name floating, and labelHidden only stops the drawing. The placeholder is never the name. The description is the input's own — the prefix and the suffix while shown, the count while counter is true — followed by what the Field gives: its supporting text with, in error, the error text after it and its optional text. The input is exposed as invalid while error is true, its Field is in error or an entry error lasts; as required while its Field says so, whichever mark is drawn; and as read-only while readOnly is true. A search input is exposed as a search box where the platform has that role. A date, time or date-time input is a group, named as the input is, whose segments are spin buttons named by their unit and that name, with a range, a value and a value text (segmentEmptyText while empty). The picker button is named by pickerLabel and exposed as opening a dialog. The resize grip is a window splitter named by resizeLabel whose value is the number of lines shown. A code input is the same text box as any other type: no role or word says that it holds code (TXI-60).
notes: Text entry happens in the platform's native element: on the web an <input> or <textarea> in the shadow root, with the label, description and invalid state set on that element — not through ElementInternals, which axe cannot see. The host is form-associated: it takes name, submits the value and joins constraint validation. A date, time or date-time field is the one exception: its segments are spin buttons that take digits one unit at a time, as the platforms' own date fields do, because one free text cannot give each unit a name, a range and a step.
Heights are minimums: at 200% text size the field grows, the floated label wraps rather than clips, and the input keeps its line height.

Web: iOS Safari zooms the page into an input whose text is smaller than 16 px. Both default sizes use 16 px text (comp.input-box.input.typescale); a layer that sets a smaller style brings the zoom back.

A trailing action (clear, reveal password, voice input) is the product's own icon-only Button, with its own accessible name in the product's language. The field builds none in except a date or time field's picker button, which the product names with pickerLabel, because each needs a localized name and a policy the field cannot know.

A date or a time is entered unit by unit: each segment says what it is, shows its own placeholder and cannot hold a value outside its range, so the format never has to be explained or remembered (WCAG 3.3.2), and a whole date can still be pasted. The picker is an alternative, never the only way.

Resizing by hand never depends on a drag (WCAG 2.5.7): the grip is a focus stop that the arrow keys move, and a click, a tap, Enter or Space fits the field to its text. Its hit area meets the minimum target although its glyph is small (WCAG 2.5.8).
A field that follows its text changes height with a short motion; where motion is reduced it changes at once (WCAG 2.3.3).
How a state looks is a value decision of the active design system; components read the state's tokens and never compute the effect themselves.

The input has no label row and no message of its own: a Field frames it and draws them (FLD-2 to FLD-11, FLD-25 to FLD-28), or the product names it with label where its visible label is elsewhere. Unframed and unnamed, it is reported (TXI-23).

Code is not prose (type code): it is left to right in every language, so a code field's input line keeps that direction and begins at the left while the label, the icons and the messages follow the page (TXI-53); and the platform's help for prose — spelling marks, autocorrection, capitals, curved quotation marks — changes or misreports it, so the field asks for none (TXI-55).

Tab always leaves a code field (WCAG 2.1.2). A field that indents with Tab needs a way out, words that say what it is, and a state that assistive technology is told — an editor's contract, which a product that embeds an editor takes on with it.

A code field whose lines do not wrap scrolls in two directions inside its container; the page never does (WCAG 1.4.10 allows it for content whose lines carry meaning). The caret is how the keyboard scrolls it, so a value that nobody may edit but that must be read whole is readOnly, not disabled, or is a Code block.

A screen reader reads punctuation and capitals in a code field as the person has set it to: the field cannot and does not change that. Color carries nothing in a code field — no part of the code is colored by its meaning — so nothing is lost in forced colors (TXI-61).

web.name: tanrei-text-input
web.notes: The input without the frame: the class `TanreiTextInput`, React `TextInput`. The host is `display: block` and as wide as its place, framed and bare (TXI-63): a Field keeps an inline-level control at its own size, at the start edge, so an inline host would not fill its Field. A form-associated custom element with a shadow root and `delegatesFocus` that takes `name`, submits its value, restores it and reports validity (a missing value while its Field says it is required; for date, time and date-time also badInput, rangeUnderflow and rangeOverflow while an entry error lasts, TXI-30). It renders an `<input>`, or a `<textarea>` while multiline, or the `role="group"` of spin buttons of a date or a time; the `leading-icon` and `trailing-icon` slots are named slots; the picker button is a `<tanrei-button variant="text">` in the shadow root. What the text field's note says of the inner element, of the types, of the segments, of the grip, of `noWrap` (attribute `no-wrap`, the inverse of `wrap`) and of code holds here for this element, with `--tanrei-comp-input-box-*` for the box (TXI-68) and `--tanrei-comp-text-input-*` for what is the text input's own. Parts: `container`, `outline`, `active-indicator`, `label` (the floating label), `requirement-label` (its asterisk), `input`, `segment`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `leading-icon`, `trailing-icon`, `picker-button`, `resize-grip`. The connection with a Field is `tanrei-field-connect` (`src/primitives/field.ts`), in both directions (TXI-62): the control's side gains what it says of itself — `drawsLabel`, `inset: { start, end }` (lengths written by the input from its own tokens and its measured icon boxes), `refusal: { text }` — and the frame's side gains `labelHidden` and `requiredMark` (`asterisk` or `none`) beside the name, the description and the three states; a Field that does not read the three ignores them, and an input no Field answers is drawn as a bare one. The count is not in the exchange: `countText` is a read-only property of the element (the text of TXI-19, empty while `counter` is false), new after each of the element's updates, which a composed element reads as it reads the value and a product reads in its own `input` listener. The routine of TXI-37 and TXI-38 that measures the lines and moves the height is one file, `src/primitives/auto-height.ts`, which draws nothing and reads no token; the web's tests of the height are one suite, so that another element that types on several lines is held to the same behaviour. The name, the description, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required` and `aria-readonly` are written on the inner element, the input's own `label` winning. Attributes are kebab-case (`label-hidden`, `min-rows`, `max-rows`, `prefix-text`, `suffix-text`, `invalid-text`, `unavailable-text`, `picker-label`, `resize-axis`, `resize-label`, `disabled-dates`, `segment-empty-text`, `no-wrap`) except `readonly`, `maxlength`, `autocomplete`, `min` and `max`, which keep HTML's names. `input` and `change` are composed events; `action` is cancelable; `pickerrequest` and `entryerror` are composed CustomEvents whose `detail` carries `{ value, type, min, max }` and `{ reason, text }`. Words: `resize-label` and `segment-empty-text` left empty read the product's words (`setWords()`). For the types email, url, tel, number and password the row of prefix, input and suffix takes the direction TXI-67 gives as its own `dir`; for every other type it keeps the host's.

swiftui.name: TanreiTextInput
swiftui.notes: Planned: this platform has the text field as one view, the frame and the input together. It owes the input as a view of its own, with the names its text field uses today for these props; the Field around it gives the name, the description and the states through the platform's own channel, and the input says what it draws back up (TXI-62).
